page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 virtual CPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.2 GHz across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it includes a large 480 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (Tile and INT8), and cryptographic acceleration instructions such as VAES and SHA-NI. The instance includes 1890 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and lacks discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results place the CPU within the average performance band across standard stress tests, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 34,203.68 and a PassMark CPU score of 48,743.5. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.05 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth achieved 146.04 GB/sec against 62.52 GB/sec for write throughput. In LLM inference tests, prompt processing for a medium 7B model scored in the top 25% at 190.8 tokens/sec, while large 70B text generation landed in the lower quartile at 2.69 tokens/sec due to the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators.

By combining 256 GB of RAM, integrated high-speed local NVMe storage, and dedicated enterprise compute cores, the E32ds_v7 functions as an efficient consolidated platform for memory-intensive workloads. It is directly suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching services like Redis, big data processing frameworks, and enterprise database systems requiring low-latency scratch disk access.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C x86_64 processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Configured with 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores with multithreading), 256.0 GB of RAM, and a 480 MB L3 cache, it delivers an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside 1890 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor supports advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark metrics reflect solid enterprise performance across the board, including top-quartile results in single-threaded gzip compression (36.05 GB/sec) and medium-model LLM prompt processing (190.8 tokens/sec), balanced by average general multi-core compute marks. The instance includes no discrete GPUs, prioritizing CPU-driven memory density and NVMe throughput. This architecture makes it well matched for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, data analytics, and memory-heavy enterprise backend workloads.
